title: Canonical Grammar Verdict
statement: Let $F$ be a machine format, and let $\alpha$, $bits$, and $rest$ be Boolean words. Suppose parsing $\alpha$ as a pair gives $(bits,rest)$, the word $bits$ is the canonical little-endian binary representation of its value $n$, and the remaining word has length at least $B(n+1)$, where $B$ is the maximum of the format's guard constant and $(4k+5)3^{k+1}$, with $k$ the format's work-tape count. If the grammar check on $n$ and $rest$ fails, decoding $\alpha$ gives the format's fallback code. If the grammar check succeeds, scanning $\alpha$ returns some suffix.
hypotheses_covered: $bits$ is the canonical little-endian binary representation of its value
The length of $rest$ is at least the guard-block bound times one more than that value
